1355	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj (Opposite.op (Over.mk (l ≫ (PicScheme C).hom))) :=

1357	-- axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
1358	```

SUMMARY:
Riemann--Roch, divisors, and the adelic genus.

Cluster-P substrate, all sorry-free and axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]:

(a) UNCONDITIONAL class invariance (Adelic/ClassInvariance.lean) -- multiplication by g is a
    k-linear automorphism of K(X) carrying chart sections, coboundary and overlap onto their
    shifted counterparts, so ell, h1 and chi are functions of the linear-equivalence class, with
    no gate, no finiteness and no ledger-exactness input.

(b) UNCONDITIONAL degree and drop bounds (Adelic/SectionBounds.lean) -- deg_k as a bundled
    AddMonoidHom, residue-degree positivity, positive degree for nonzero effective divisors, and
    the drop sandwich ell(D) <= ell(D+P) <= ell(D)+[kappa(P):k].

(c) THE CLOSED CHI-LEDGER, PROVED (Adelic/LedgerClosure.chi_eq_of_bump, run 0055 s0008) --
    chi(D) = chi(0) + deg_k D at EVERY Weil divisor, from the one-point bump alone. This was
    recorded as open by three sessions, with a correct-but-irrelevant obstruction argument; the
    resolution is that hbump admits an ARBITRARY base divisor, so the telescope runs onto the
    base D rather than up from 0. hledger is therefore no longer an independent lane input, and
    six ledger-free restatements of the lane's conclusions are in LedgerClosure section 2.

(d) CONDITIONAL single-field bounded H1 vanishing (Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean) --
    exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod, b = deg_k D0 + 1 - chi(0). Open inputs now TWO, not three,
    and both are one-point local statements: the bump, and the one-point peel. The peel is FREE
    off the overlap (peel_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap), so its content sits at overlap points
    only -- a small saving, since the overlap of a 2-affine cover of an irreducible curve is dense.

(e) PROVED global generation (Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean) -- the evaluation map
    Gamma(D)/Gamma(D-P) -> kappa(P) is onto exactly when the section drop is maximal, which the
    ledger converts into a PAIR of vanishings. Conditional on the same inputs as (d).

(f) THE RESIDUE LANE, CLOSED (Adelic/ResidueField.lean) -- residueDeg = 1 and node N14's
    residue-finiteness gate both DISCHARGED on curve hypotheses; deg_k = deg unconditional;
    ell(D) = deg D + 1 - g for deg large on the GEOMETRIC degree.

THE THREE GAPS, KEPT APART (the task requires this separation):
  1. single-field vanishing -- conditional on the bump, one base vanishing, and the overlap peel;

data.content:
With `proj = 𝟙` the universal property degenerates to `∃! u, 𝟙 ≫ u = h`. So the bare
structure is nearly free, and exhibiting *some* `SymPowData` proves nothing.

What the downstream theorems actually quantify over is the **pair**
`(D, hproj)`, where `hproj : ∀ σ, permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj` says the projection
is genuinely symmetric. The `proj := 𝟙` trick fails that whenever `permAut C σ ≠ 𝟙`, which
for `n ≥ 2` holds as soon as `C` has two distinct global points — the case of interest, and
proved in `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` (`permAut_swap_ne_id_of_points`). It is *not*
automatic from `n ≥ 2` alone: at a **terminal** `C` the trivial datum does satisfy `hproj`
at every `n` (`permAut_eq_id_of_isTerminal`), so an unqualified "fails for `n ≥ 2`" is
false. So the pair is the meaningful object away from that degenerate case, and this file
witnesses it for `n = 1`: `symPowDataOne` plus `symPowDataOne_proj_perm`.

Two honest caveats about that witness:

morphism out of `C^1` — symmetric or not, since `S_1` is trivial — factors uniquely
through it.

For `n ≥ 2`, inhabiting `SymPowData` *together with the symmetry hypothesis* is equivalent
to a colimit of the `S_n`-action (`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean`) — proved for affine
`k`-schemes at every `n`, still open for a proper curve. -/
noncomputable def symPowDataOne (C : K) : SymPowData C 1 where
`SymPowData C n` is inhabited for *every* `n` by taking `proj := 𝟙`, which makes the
universal property vacuous. This declaration exists so that the limitation is a checked
fact in the tree rather than a remark someone might doubt or forget.

Its purpose is contrastive: a downstream theorem is only meaningful because it *also*
requires `hproj : ∀ σ, permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj`, which this datum **fails** whenever
`permAut C σ ≠ 𝟙` — for `n ≥ 2` that holds as soon as `C` has two distinct global points
(`permAut_swap_ne_id_of_points`), though **not** at a terminal `C`, where it genuinely
satisfies `hproj` (`permAut_eq_id_of_isTerminal`); both in
`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean`. Do not use it for anything; if a future
lemma over `SymPowData` can be instantiated at `symPowDataTrivial`, that lemma is

task show --json OMITS THE comments KEY ENTIRELY, so a lane verifying its own task comment by read-back concludes the write FAILED when it landed. Measured run 0070 s0010 (ajcr-cert-r2), 2026-07-28.

THE DEFECT, and it is in the READER not the writer:
 * 'horizon task comment <id> --body ...' exits 0 and prints '[HORIZON] OK Commented on task <id>'. The write DOES land: .archon-horizon/tasks/comments/<task-id>/C-000N.md is created with correct frontmatter (id, item, author, at, full provenance) and body.
 * 'horizon task show <id> --json' returns keys [id, project, projects, title, objective, status, priority, write_set, scope, roadmap_refs, inbox_refs, warnings] -- NO 'comments' key, not even an empty list. The plain (non-JSON) 'task show' likewise prints no comment section.
 * By contrast 'inbox show <id> --json' DOES return 'comments', so the two subsystems disagree and a lane reasonably expects the task one to behave the same way.

WHY IT MATTERS RIGHT NOW: I-0609 and I-0612 established the opposite failure -- writes that silently do NOT land (the 1200-char comment cap, whose rejection is the last line after ~25 lines of banner). A lane that has internalised those items will read-back-verify, see no comments key, and conclude its write was silently dropped. That is a FALSE POSITIVE for I-0609, and the wrong response to it (re-issuing the comment) creates duplicates. I nearly filed one.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, cheap and reliable: ls .archon-horizon/tasks/comments/<task-id>/ and read the newest C-*.md, checking the 'session:' provenance line is yours. Disk is the truth; task show is blind to it. My eight comments on ajcr-cert-r2 are all on disk while task show --json reports zero.

TWO DEFECTS, ONE ITEM, and they should be fixed together: (1) task show should surface comments in both renderings; (2) if the omission is deliberate, the 1200-char cap message on task comment should say where the comment can be read back, since it is the only comment-related feedback a caller gets.

FOR NOW, the binding practical rule for any lane: verify a TASK comment on disk, not via task show. Verify an INBOX comment via inbox show --json, which works.
